I'm not sure that making college free is going to solve many problems, and in fact, it might make new ones.

Simply put, having a more educated population is not going to help with the job market the way people think it will. It's something of a treadmill - the more people are educated, the more people are going to be competing for X many higher-end jobs, and then even more people with higher qualifications competing for lower-end jobs. The people who can't cut it in college suffer more because you have people with bachelor's degrees competing to do their jobs. As a result you have just as much unemployment as well as more people who are effectively permanently unemployed. Meanwhile on the other end, you have a glut of people who sat in college for 4-10 years, and now you've got people with Ph.D.'s doing burger flipping, because there are still only so many slots for the high-end degrees, and the overall increase in availability of degrees has likely outpaced the increase in slots for those advanced degrees. This is made even worse as robots and mechanical solutions are phased in to replace human workers for lower-skill jobs, resulting in what amounts to working people to death overeducating them for jobs that do not require that level of knowledge, and a permanently unemployable underclass struggling to survive.

I don't know what the solution is, or if there even is a solution, but long-term, college is no panacea.
